bull_bear.body:
- Twenty-five years of deep healthcare software domain expertise, which management describes as the natural synergy anchoring the build-out of the AI-led healthcare use cases in the Emerging Technologies vertical
- Proprietary, Microsoft-certified IP-based vertical solutions (Quality Management, Plant Maintenance, HR & Payroll localized for multiple countries, Pharmaceutical ERP, Budget Control Extensions, Publishing Industry Vertical) that differentiate the ERP business from generic implementation services
- Installed base of more than 200 ERP customers across pharmaceuticals, manufacturing, publishing, finance, supply chain, healthcare, engineering and life sciences, which the outlook expects the ERP Division to stabilize around
- Microsoft partner status - the Company states it advances and adds value to Microsoft's business solutions and client relationships
- International delivery footprint spanning the United States, Australia, Singapore, Malaysia, the Philippines, South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria, Mauritius, Belgium, the UAE, Vietnam and Sri Lanka
- A long-term AI implementation engagement with Antelope Valley Cancer Centre, cited as a proof point of capability to deliver large-scale AI-enabled healthcare transformation and expected to serve as a reference engagement
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Competitive intensity and pricing pressure in the Microsoft Dynamics ERP ecosystem — Management lists 'intensifying competition within the Microsoft Dynamics ecosystem, particularly affecting ERP Division margins' and 'pricing pressures impacting operating margins, most notably within the legacy ERP business' under Risks and Concerns. The MD&A confirms this is already live rather than prospective: the ERP Division 'experienced a moderating revenue trajectory and margin compression during the year', reflecting pricing pressure on implementation and support contracts and the natural maturation of several long-standing client engagements. The broader on-premise/legacy ERP implementation market is described as maturing and facing pricing and margin pressure.
- Execution risk on the pivot to the Emerging Technologies (AI, ML, Cybersecurity) vertical — The Company is deliberately rebalancing toward a division established only in 2024-25/2025-26, directing a disproportionate share of capital expenditure, talent and go-to-market investment into it while consciously moderating the ERP Division's share of the growth strategy. That vertical is expected to be the principal driver of revenue and margin expansion over the medium term, so the outlook depends on an unproven business reaching scale. The upfront investment in scaling it, together with a higher effective tax charge, is cited as the reason net profit margin declined at both standalone and consolidated levels, and normalization is contingent on the vertical 'achieving operating scale'.
- Rapid technological change in AI/ML requiring continuous reinvestment — Listed under both Threats and Risks and Concerns as the 'rapid pace of technological change in AI/ML requiring sustained and continuous investment to remain competitive' and 'requiring continuous innovation and re-skilling'. For a company whose growth thesis rests on this vertical, the obsolescence cycle is a recurring, non-discretionary claim on capital and management attention rather than a one-time cost.
- Competition for specialised AI, ML and cybersecurity talent — Flagged explicitly as both a threat and a risk: 'talent acquisition and retention in specialized technology domains, especially AI, ML and cybersecurity'. Delivery capacity in a services business is headcount-bound, and the HR section confirms a particular emphasis on building specialised AI, ML and cybersecurity talent to support the strategic pivot - making hiring and retention the binding constraint on the Company's stated growth engine.
- Global macroeconomic uncertainty affecting customer IT spending — Listed under both Threats and Risks and Concerns. The MD&A opens on moderate global growth amid geopolitical uncertainties, inflationary pressures, elevated interest rates and slowing international trade. Discretionary enterprise IT budgets - ERP implementations and AI projects alike - are the first line item deferred in a spending slowdown, and the Cautionary Statement names economic conditions affecting demand/supply as a factor that could make actual results differ materially.
- Cybersecurity threats and evolving regulatory requirements — Named in both the Threats and the Risks and Concerns lists as the 'evolving cybersecurity threat landscape and regulatory requirements'. The exposure is double-sided: the Company handles US healthcare data through the GeniusDoc EMR platform (subject to HIPAA), and it simultaneously sells cybersecurity, cyber audit, HIPAA compliance and privacy assessment services, so a security or compliance failure would carry commercial credibility consequences beyond the direct incident.
- Concentration in the US healthcare market and a single EMR platform — The Healthcare Division's described activity is software development, product enhancement, maintenance, AI integration and analytics for the GeniusDoc Electronic Medical Records platform in the United States, and the Emerging Technologies build-out is anchored on AI-led healthcare use cases with a single named reference engagement (Antelope Valley Cancer Centre) expected to serve as the model for similar opportunities. Growth is therefore concentrated on one geography, one healthcare platform relationship and one flagship engagement. Management's stated mitigation is to 'diversify its customer base' alongside strengthening its IP portfolio.
- Share-capital/compliance matter flagged by the auditor as an Emphasis of Matter — The auditor draws attention to Note 48, describing the Company's filing of Form PAS-3 on March 25, 2025 for allotment of 4,00,000 equity shares under the ESOP Trust route and the Board's subsequent decision to withdraw that allotment. The Company represented that no options were granted or exercised, that the allotment has been reversed and not given effect to in the financial statements, and that an application to the Registrar of Companies for cancellation of the filing remains pending as at the date of the report. The auditor's opinion is not modified in respect of this matter, but the regulatory cancellation is unresolved at the reporting date.

business.body: The Company builds and supports healthcare software and Microsoft Dynamics ERP solutions for mid-sized companies and larger enterprises, and over the last two years has invested to build an Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Cybersecurity capability. Its Healthcare Division provides software development, product enhancement, maintenance, AI integration and advanced analytics for the GeniusDoc Electronic Medical Records platform in the United States, spanning EMR, Practice Management, Revenue Cycle Management, EPCS, Population Health Management, Telehealth, Healthcare Analytics and EDI. The Enterprise ERP Division provides Microsoft Dynamics implementation, consulting, customization, cloud migration and support, differentiated through domain- and vertical-specific proprietary IP rather than generic implementation services.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Healthcare Solutions:** GeniusDoc Electronic Medical Records (EMR) platform, Practice Management (PM), Revenue Cycle Management (RCM), Electronic Prescribing of Controlled Substances (EPCS), Population Health Management, Telehealth solutions, Healthcare Analytics, Electronic Data Interchange (EDI), AI-enabled clinical documentation with Voice-to-Text conversion, NLP-based physician assistance, AI-powered Clinical Decision Support Systems, Precision Medicine and Oncology Analytics, Intelligent chatbot agents for healthcare workflows, Mobile healthcare applications
- **Emerging Technologies - AI, ML and Cybersecurity:** Artificial Intelligence, Large Language Models (LLMs) and Deep Learning, AI-powered Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) insights, LLM-integrated enterprise and clinical workflows, Cybersecurity and Cyber Audits for Healthcare and ERP environments (HIPAA compliance and privacy assessments, threat intelligence, vulnerability scanning), Cloud migration to Azure, AWS, Google Cloud and Oracle Cloud, Robotic Process Automation (RPA), Blockchain applications, Data Warehousing, Data Mining and Advanced Analytics, Internet of Things (IoT), Low-code and no-code development tools, Agentic Chatbots
- **Enterprise ERP Solutions:** Microsoft Dynamics ERP implementation, consulting, customization, cloud migration and support, Quality Management add-on, Plant Maintenance add-on, HR & Payroll solutions localized for multiple countries, Pharmaceutical ERP Vertical Solution, Budget Control Extensions, Publishing Industry Vertical Solution for Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, Life Sciences Vertical for Microsoft Dynamics NAV and AX

outlook.body:
- Reorganise the business around three strategic verticals - Healthcare Solutions, Emerging Technologies (AI, ML and Cybersecurity) and Enterprise ERP Solutions - and treat the Emerging Technologies Division, established in 2024-25/2025-26, as the primary growth engine going forward.
- Deliberately build the Emerging Technologies Division with an initial and deepening focus on AI-led healthcare use cases, exploiting the synergy with the Company's twenty-five-year healthcare domain expertise, while extending into cybersecurity and cloud-native transformation for enterprise clients.
- Direct a disproportionate share of capital expenditure, talent acquisition and go-to-market investment toward the AI/ML/Cybersecurity vertical over the medium term, given the addressable opportunity relative to the more mature ERP market.
- Consciously moderate the relative share of the legacy Microsoft Dynamics ERP Division within the overall growth strategy while continuing to service and invest selectively in it, preserving legacy value, client relationships and proprietary IP.
- Differentiate the ERP business through domain- and vertical-specific proprietary IP (Quality Management, Plant Maintenance, HR & Payroll localized for multiple countries, Pharmaceutical ERP, Budget Control Extensions, Publishing Industry Vertical for Dynamics 365 Business Central) rather than generic implementation services.
- Commercialize proprietary vertical solutions through Microsoft AppSource, starting with the Publishing Industry Vertical Solution, to create an incremental higher-margin recurring revenue stream.
- Use the Antelope Valley Cancer Centre long-term AI implementation engagement as a reference model and scale that engagement model to other healthcare providers.
- Strengthen the intellectual property portfolio, diversify the customer base and rebalance the investment mix toward higher-growth verticals as the stated mitigation for competitive and technology risks.
- Build specialized AI, ML and cybersecurity talent through technical skill development, leadership programmes and AI/cloud technology certifications to support the pivot toward Emerging Technologies.
- Pursue growth across India, the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia alongside the established US and international ERP footprint.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: B2B Software Technologies is an asset-light IT services company and discloses no plants or manufacturing capacity; its expansion during FY 2025-26 was the build-out of a new Emerging Technologies Division. The Directors' Report states the Company established a new Division for 'Emerging Technologies' to address demand for AI, Machine Learning, Large Language Models, Agentic Chatbots, Blockchain, Robotic Process Automation, digital workflow transformation, data mining and warehousing, advanced analytics, low-code/no-code tools, cloud migration and cybersecurity, and that the initial capital expenditure for the launch of this division has been approved at Rs. 1 crore, to be funded from internal accruals with provision for additional funding as required. The new division commenced operations from September 2025 with the required infrastructure setup. The MD&A adds that the Company intends to continue directing a disproportionate share of capital expenditure, talent acquisition and go-to-market investment toward this vertical over the medium term, and that upfront investment in scaling it weighed on net profit margin during the year and is expected to normalize as the vertical achieves operating scale. Other expansion is footprint- and IP-led rather than capacity-led: ERP operations extend across the United States, Australia, Singapore, Malaysia, the Philippines, South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria, Mauritius, Belgium, the UAE, Vietnam and Sri Lanka, with stated growth opportunities across India, the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia; and significant progress was made during the year toward publishing the Publishing Industry Vertical Solution on Microsoft AppSource. The Company has one subsidiary as on March 31, 2026 - B2B Softech INC, USA - and no company became or ceased to be a subsidiary, joint venture or associate during the year. The accounts state there are no capital commitments as on 31st March, 2026 (previous year NIL).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Growing enterprise investment in cloud computing, cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence, healthcare digitization and automation is stated to create significant opportunities for technology solution providers such as the Company.
- Healthcare organizations are increasingly adopting AI-enabled clinical systems, advanced analytics, telehealth and digital patient-engagement platforms.
- Enterprises across sectors continue to migrate to cloud-based ERP platforms and invest in automation, cybersecurity and AI-powered decision-support systems.
- Microsoft Dynamics 365 continues to gain market acceptance globally, creating opportunities for implementation partners with industry-specific expertise and proprietary IP.
- The broader on-premise/legacy ERP implementation market is maturing and faces pricing and margin pressure - a headwind management explicitly attaches to its own ERP Division.
- Management expects the Emerging Technologies - AI, ML and Cybersecurity vertical to be the principal driver of revenue and margin expansion over the medium term, anchored in deep healthcare domain expertise.
- The Healthcare Division is expected to continue its steady growth trajectory, supported by AI-enabled product enhancements.
- The ERP Division is expected to stabilize around its core installed base of over 200 customers and its proprietary vertical IP, even as its relative contribution to overall growth moderates further.
- Management expects investments in AI, cloud technologies, industry-specific IP and healthcare innovation to support sustainable long-term growth and margin improvement at the consolidated level.
- Margin lever/drag: the moderate decline in net profit margin is attributed to a higher effective tax charge and the upfront investment in scaling the AI/ML/Cybersecurity vertical, and is expected to normalize as that vertical achieves operating scale.
- Mix: revenue growth is stated to be driven principally by the Healthcare and Emerging Technologies verticals, partly offset by the moderating ERP Division.
- Publishing the Publishing Industry Vertical Solution on Microsoft AppSource is expected to create an incremental, higher-margin recurring revenue stream that partially offsets broader ERP margin pressure.
- Global macroeconomic uncertainty affecting customer IT spending is flagged as a demand-side threat.
- Rising demand for cybersecurity, HIPAA compliance and regulatory-driven audit services is cited as an opportunity.
- Qualitative pipeline mention only: 'Expansion of the AI/ML services pipeline, including scaling of the Antelope Valley Cancer Centre engagement model to other healthcare providers.' The Company also refers to a long-term AI implementation engagement with Antelope Valley Cancer Centre expected to serve as a reference engagement for similar opportunities. No order-book value, contract value or duration is disclosed.
- Installed base reference rather than an order book: ERP solutions successfully implemented for more than 200 customers, around which the ERP Division is expected to stabilize.

one_liner.body: B2B Software Technologies is a twenty-five-year-old technology solutions company focused on Healthcare Information Systems and Enterprise Digital Transformation, now organised around three verticals - Healthcare Solutions, Emerging Technologies (AI/ML/Cybersecurity) and Microsoft Dynamics …

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company builds and supports healthcare software and Microsoft Dynamics ERP solutions for mid-sized companies and larger enterprises, and over the last two years has invested to build an Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Cybersecurity capability. Its Healthcare Division provides software development, product enhancement, maintenance, AI integration and advanced analytics for the GeniusDoc Electronic Medical Records platform in the United States, spanning EMR, Practice Management, Revenue Cycle Management, EPCS, Population Health Management, Telehealth, Healthcare Analytics and EDI. The Enterprise ERP Division provides Microsoft Dynamics implementation, consulting, customization, cloud migration and support, differentiated through domain- and vertical-specific proprietary IP rather than generic implementation services.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- B2B Softech Inc., USA — subsidiary: The Company's only subsidiary as on March 31, 2026; listed in Form AOC-1 Part A as acquired since July 17, 2001, with USD as its reporting currency and no reporting period different from the holding company's. Also listed in the Ind-AS 24 related-party note under 'Parties where control exist' as Subsidiary Company. The Directors' Report states no company became or ceased to be a subsidiary, joint venture or associate during the year, and no subsidiary is yet to commence operations or was liquidated or sold during the year.

The GeniusDoc Electronic Medical Records platform is the product the Company's Healthcare Division develops, enhances and maintains in the United States.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Growing enterprise investment in cloud computing, cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence, healthcare digitization and automation is stated to create significant opportunities for technology solution providers such as the Company.
- Healthcare organizations are increasingly adopting AI-enabled clinical systems, advanced analytics, telehealth and digital patient-engagement platforms.
- Enterprises across sectors continue to migrate to cloud-based ERP platforms and invest in automation, cybersecurity and AI-powered decision-support systems.
- Microsoft Dynamics 365 continues to gain market acceptance globally, creating opportunities for implementation partners with industry-specific expertise and proprietary IP.
- The broader on-premise/legacy ERP implementation market is maturing and faces pricing and margin pressure - a headwind management explicitly attaches to its own ERP Division.
- Management expects the Emerging Technologies - AI, ML and Cybersecurity vertical to be the principal driver of revenue and margin expansion over the medium term, anchored in deep healthcare domain expertise.
- The Healthcare Division is expected to continue its steady growth trajectory, supported by AI-enabled product enhancements.
- The ERP Division is expected to stabilize around its core installed base of over 200 customers and its proprietary vertical IP, even as its relative contribution to overall growth moderates further.
- Management expects investments in AI, cloud technologies, industry-specific IP and healthcare innovation to support sustainable long-term growth and margin improvement at the consolidated level.
- Margin lever/drag: the moderate decline in net profit margin is attributed to a higher effective tax charge and the upfront investment in scaling the AI/ML/Cybersecurity vertical, and is expected to normalize as that vertical achieves operating scale.
- Mix: revenue growth is stated to be driven principally by the Healthcare and Emerging Technologies verticals, partly offset by the moderating ERP Division.
- Publishing the Publishing Industry Vertical Solution on Microsoft AppSource is expected to create an incremental, higher-margin recurring revenue stream that partially offsets broader ERP margin pressure.
- Global macroeconomic uncertainty affecting customer IT spending is flagged as a demand-side threat.
- Rising demand for cybersecurity, HIPAA compliance and regulatory-driven audit services is cited as an opportunity.
- Qualitative pipeline mention only: 'Expansion of the AI/ML services pipeline, including scaling of the Antelope Valley Cancer Centre engagement model to other healthcare providers.' The Company also refers to a long-term AI implementation engagement with Antelope Valley Cancer Centre expected to serve as a reference engagement for similar opportunities. No order-book value, contract value or duration is disclosed.
- Installed base reference rather than an order book: ERP solutions successfully implemented for more than 200 customers, around which the ERP Division is expected to stabilize.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Reorganise the business around three strategic verticals - Healthcare Solutions, Emerging Technologies (AI, ML and Cybersecurity) and Enterprise ERP Solutions - and treat the Emerging Technologies Division, established in 2024-25/2025-26, as the primary growth engine going forward.
- Deliberately build the Emerging Technologies Division with an initial and deepening focus on AI-led healthcare use cases, exploiting the synergy with the Company's twenty-five-year healthcare domain expertise, while extending into cybersecurity and cloud-native transformation for enterprise clients.
- Direct a disproportionate share of capital expenditure, talent acquisition and go-to-market investment toward the AI/ML/Cybersecurity vertical over the medium term, given the addressable opportunity relative to the more mature ERP market.
- Consciously moderate the relative share of the legacy Microsoft Dynamics ERP Division within the overall growth strategy while continuing to service and invest selectively in it, preserving legacy value, client relationships and proprietary IP.
- Differentiate the ERP business through domain- and vertical-specific proprietary IP (Quality Management, Plant Maintenance, HR & Payroll localized for multiple countries, Pharmaceutical ERP, Budget Control Extensions, Publishing Industry Vertical for Dynamics 365 Business Central) rather than generic implementation services.
- Commercialize proprietary vertical solutions through Microsoft AppSource, starting with the Publishing Industry Vertical Solution, to create an incremental higher-margin recurring revenue stream.
- Use the Antelope Valley Cancer Centre long-term AI implementation engagement as a reference model and scale that engagement model to other healthcare providers.
- Strengthen the intellectual property portfolio, diversify the customer base and rebalance the investment mix toward higher-growth verticals as the stated mitigation for competitive and technology risks.
- Build specialized AI, ML and cybersecurity talent through technical skill development, leadership programmes and AI/cloud technology certifications to support the pivot toward Emerging Technologies.
- Pursue growth across India, the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia alongside the established US and international ERP footprint.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: B2B Software Technologies is an asset-light IT services company and discloses no plants or manufacturing capacity; its expansion during FY 2025-26 was the build-out of a new Emerging Technologies Division. The Directors' Report states the Company established a new Division for 'Emerging Technologies' to address demand for AI, Machine Learning, Large Language Models, Agentic Chatbots, Blockchain, Robotic Process Automation, digital workflow transformation, data mining and warehousing, advanced analytics, low-code/no-code tools, cloud migration and cybersecurity, and that the initial capital expenditure for the launch of this division has been approved at Rs. 1 crore, to be funded from internal accruals with provision for additional funding as required. The new division commenced operations from September 2025 with the required infrastructure setup. The MD&A adds that the Company intends to continue directing a disproportionate share of capital expenditure, talent acquisition and go-to-market investment toward this vertical over the medium term, and that upfront investment in scaling it weighed on net profit margin during the year and is expected to normalize as the vertical achieves operating scale. Other expansion is footprint- and IP-led rather than capacity-led: ERP operations extend across the United States, Australia, Singapore, Malaysia, the Philippines, South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria, Mauritius, Belgium, the UAE, Vietnam and Sri Lanka, with stated growth opportunities across India, the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia; and significant progress was made during the year toward publishing the Publishing Industry Vertical Solution on Microsoft AppSource. The Company has one subsidiary as on March 31, 2026 - B2B Softech INC, USA - and no company became or ceased to be a subsidiary, joint venture or associate during the year. The accounts state there are no capital commitments as on 31st March, 2026 (previous year NIL).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Twenty-five years of deep healthcare software domain expertise, which management describes as the natural synergy anchoring the build-out of the AI-led healthcare use cases in the Emerging Technologies vertical
- Proprietary, Microsoft-certified IP-based vertical solutions (Quality Management, Plant Maintenance, HR & Payroll localized for multiple countries, Pharmaceutical ERP, Budget Control Extensions, Publishing Industry Vertical) that differentiate the ERP business from generic implementation services
- Installed base of more than 200 ERP customers across pharmaceuticals, manufacturing, publishing, finance, supply chain, healthcare, engineering and life sciences, which the outlook expects the ERP Division to stabilize around
- Microsoft partner status - the Company states it advances and adds value to Microsoft's business solutions and client relationships
- International delivery footprint spanning the United States, Australia, Singapore, Malaysia, the Philippines, South Africa, Kenya, Nigeria, Mauritius, Belgium, the UAE, Vietnam and Sri Lanka
- A long-term AI implementation engagement with Antelope Valley Cancer Centre, cited as a proof point of capability to deliver large-scale AI-enabled healthcare transformation and expected to serve as a reference engagement

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Competitive intensity and pricing pressure in the Microsoft Dynamics ERP ecosystem — Management lists 'intensifying competition within the Microsoft Dynamics ecosystem, particularly affecting ERP Division margins' and 'pricing pressures impacting operating margins, most notably within the legacy ERP business' under Risks and Concerns. The MD&A confirms this is already live rather than prospective: the ERP Division 'experienced a moderating revenue trajectory and margin compression during the year', reflecting pricing pressure on implementation and support contracts and the natural maturation of several long-standing client engagements. The broader on-premise/legacy ERP implementation market is described as maturing and facing pricing and margin pressure.
- Execution risk on the pivot to the Emerging Technologies (AI, ML, Cybersecurity) vertical — The Company is deliberately rebalancing toward a division established only in 2024-25/2025-26, directing a disproportionate share of capital expenditure, talent and go-to-market investment into it while consciously moderating the ERP Division's share of the growth strategy. That vertical is expected to be the principal driver of revenue and margin expansion over the medium term, so the outlook depends on an unproven business reaching scale. The upfront investment in scaling it, together with a higher effective tax charge, is cited as the reason net profit margin declined at both standalone and consolidated levels, and normalization is contingent on the vertical 'achieving operating scale'.
- Rapid technological change in AI/ML requiring continuous reinvestment — Listed under both Threats and Risks and Concerns as the 'rapid pace of technological change in AI/ML requiring sustained and continuous investment to remain competitive' and 'requiring continuous innovation and re-skilling'. For a company whose growth thesis rests on this vertical, the obsolescence cycle is a recurring, non-discretionary claim on capital and management attention rather than a one-time cost.
- Competition for specialised AI, ML and cybersecurity talent — Flagged explicitly as both a threat and a risk: 'talent acquisition and retention in specialized technology domains, especially AI, ML and cybersecurity'. Delivery capacity in a services business is headcount-bound, and the HR section confirms a particular emphasis on building specialised AI, ML and cybersecurity talent to support the strategic pivot - making hiring and retention the binding constraint on the Company's stated growth engine.
- Global macroeconomic uncertainty affecting customer IT spending — Listed under both Threats and Risks and Concerns. The MD&A opens on moderate global growth amid geopolitical uncertainties, inflationary pressures, elevated interest rates and slowing international trade. Discretionary enterprise IT budgets - ERP implementations and AI projects alike - are the first line item deferred in a spending slowdown, and the Cautionary Statement names economic conditions affecting demand/supply as a factor that could make actual results differ materially.
- Cybersecurity threats and evolving regulatory requirements — Named in both the Threats and the Risks and Concerns lists as the 'evolving cybersecurity threat landscape and regulatory requirements'. The exposure is double-sided: the Company handles US healthcare data through the GeniusDoc EMR platform (subject to HIPAA), and it simultaneously sells cybersecurity, cyber audit, HIPAA compliance and privacy assessment services, so a security or compliance failure would carry commercial credibility consequences beyond the direct incident.
- Concentration in the US healthcare market and a single EMR platform — The Healthcare Division's described activity is software development, product enhancement, maintenance, AI integration and analytics for the GeniusDoc Electronic Medical Records platform in the United States, and the Emerging Technologies build-out is anchored on AI-led healthcare use cases with a single named reference engagement (Antelope Valley Cancer Centre) expected to serve as the model for similar opportunities. Growth is therefore concentrated on one geography, one healthcare platform relationship and one flagship engagement. Management's stated mitigation is to 'diversify its customer base' alongside strengthening its IP portfolio.
- Share-capital/compliance matter flagged by the auditor as an Emphasis of Matter — The auditor draws attention to Note 48, describing the Company's filing of Form PAS-3 on March 25, 2025 for allotment of 4,00,000 equity shares under the ESOP Trust route and the Board's subsequent decision to withdraw that allotment. The Company represented that no options were granted or exercised, that the allotment has been reversed and not given effect to in the financial statements, and that an application to the Registrar of Companies for cancellation of the filing remains pending as at the date of the report. The auditor's opinion is not modified in respect of this matter, but the regulatory cancellation is unresolved at the reporting date.
